text:
miko: heads up, seeing persistent TX queue depth spikes on eu-west-dedicated-5 since ~01:10 UTC. 99p token latency creeping.

dave: confirmed. top-of-rack shows PCIe bandwidth saturation and NVLink stalls when tenant ml-ingest-77 is active.

asha: is this from a training job or dataset pulls?

miko: looks like a mixture — lots of small RPCs + a few huge parameter fetches. p99 of small RPCs suffer when big streams start.

ryan: classic noisy-neighbor hybrid. We don't want to carve racks yet. Can we try a lightweight egress-crediting approach + packet-marking so big flows get lower priority?

dave: we prototyped eBPF cgroup marks last quarter. Quick rule to mark >100MB/s flows and attach HTB classes. Low overhead.

miko: paste of check commands i ran:
```bash
# check PCIe and tx queues
sar -n DEV 1 3 | grep eth0
cat /sys/class/net/eth0/queues/tx-0/backlog
# identify heavy flows
ss -tnp | awk '{print $5,$7}' | sort -rn | head
```

asha: what's the safe threshold? 100MB/s? 200MB/s?

dave: we measured tail crossover around 150MB/s on these racks. Suggest mark threshold = 150MB/s and soft-credit to 120MB/s for heavy class.

ryan: policy note: if we start deprioritizing flows in a dedicated pool, enterprise customers may complain. Need an opt-in charge for "priority egress". Keep default soft-credit and document SLA implications.

miko: I can roll a canary on node rack-5c with the eBPF mark + tc classes. Patch below (simplified):
```bash
# attach bpf prog to cgroup to mark flows >150MB/s
bpftool prog load ./mark_heavy.o /sys/fs/bpf/mark_heavy
tc qdisc replace dev eth0 root handle 1: htb default 20
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1: classid 1:1 htb rate 1gbit
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1:1 classid 1:10 htb rate 900mbit
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1:1 classid 1:20 htb rate 200mbit
tc filter add dev eth0 protocol ip parent 1:0 prio 1 handle 0x1 bpf
```

asha: what's the rollback?

miko: rollback is simple:
```bash
tc qdisc del dev eth0 root
bpftool prog detach // or unload
```

ryan: add metrics: per-tenant heavy-mark-count, per-class tx_bytes, p99 latency per tenant. If heavy-mark spikes, route new allocs away from that rack.

dave: Also add a passive fallback: if we detect >3 sustained heavy-mark breaches in 10m, trigger autoscheduler to avoid rack. That reduces live migration churn.

infra-bot: Incident recorded: INC-4721 - "eu-west-dedicated-5 p99 cartwheel due to egress saturation". On-call: ryan.

asha: cost modeling: if soft-credit reduces tail but increases job runtime slightly, customers on burst pricing might see higher bill. We need to simulate impact for top 10 tenants. I'll run sims and post numbers by EOD.

miko: starting canary in 10m on rack-5c. Will capture before/after dashboards and post links.

ryan: thumbs up. if canary passes (p99 reduction >40% and CPU overhead <3%), schedule region-wide roll with opt-out flag and a paid priority carveout lane.

dave: also document expected behavior in runbook: "when eBPF mark causes regressions for small RPCs, revert and increase threshold to 200MB/s". Add commands to clear marks and remove tc rules.

miko: noted. I'll open a PR with scripts, dashboards, and runbook snippets. Keeping this thread as the coordination log.

ryan: thanks all, ping here if anything flares after canary.
